record.paper_title: A New Paradigm for Scattering Theory of Linear and Nonlinear Waves: Review and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Nonlinear resonances and Fermi Golden Rule from S-matrix
record.original_question: For nonlinear systems such as a double-well potential in any dimension with an added nonlinear term, how can the corresponding resonances be determined from inverse scattering data, and how can the value of the nonlinear Fermi Golden Rule be recovered from the S-matrix?

evidence.quote: If we take a double well potential in any dimension and add a nonlinear term, how can we find the corresponding resonances? This problem involves complex dynamics where the structure of the potential governs and produces solitons Barak et al. (2008); Dekel et al. (2007, 2009). In direct scattering, we know how to handle it in some cases, using the notion of the nonlinear Fermi Golden Rule. But for inverse scattering, how can we find the value of the FGR from the S-matrix?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a Schrödinger-type evolution on $\mathbb{R}^d$ of the form
$$ i\partial_t \psi = (-\Delta + V(x))\psi + N(\psi), \qquad \psi(0,\cdot)=\psi_0,$$
where $V:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}$ is a smooth, rapidly decaying double-well potential (so that $-\Delta+V$ has at least two simple eigenvalues $e_0<e_1<0$ embedded below the continuous spectrum $[0,\infty)$), and $N$ is a smooth nonlinearity that vanishes to order $\geq 2$ at the origin (for instance $N(\psi)=\lambda|\psi|^{2}\psi$ with $\lambda\in\mathbb{R}$).

Under the nonlinear evolution, the excited bound state at energy $e_1$ is generically coupled to the continuous spectrum through the nonlinear interaction, producing a metastable (resonant) state whose decay rate is governed by a nonlinear analog of the Fermi Golden Rule (FGR): namely, a positive constant $\Gamma>0$, built from a projection of the nonlinear coupling onto the continuous spectral subspace at the resonant energy $2e_1-e_0$ (or, more generally, at an integer combination of bound state energies that lies in $[0,\infty)$), which controls the leading-order rate of energy transfer from the bound mode to radiation.

For the linear scattering problem associated with $-\Delta+V$ one has the standard scattering operator $S_L$ (acting on the asymptotic states at energy $k^2>0$). For the nonlinear problem, define a nonlinear scattering map $S_{NL}$ as the map that sends asymptotic free data at $t\to-\infty$ to asymptotic free data at $t\to+\infty$ (assumed to exist on a suitable class of small scattering states).

Problem. 
(a) Locate, in terms of the data of the nonlinear scattering map $S_{NL}$, the complex resonance energies of the perturbed system (i.e. the analogs of poles of the analytically continued scattering operator that give rise to metastable bound-state behavior).
(b) Give an explicit formula that recovers the value $\Gamma$ of the nonlinear Fermi Golden Rule from $S_{NL}$ (equivalently, from the inverse scattering data of the nonlinear problem), without prior knowledge of $V$ or $N$.
artifact.status_search_result: Standard references discuss the nonlinear Fermi Golden Rule in the direct scattering setting (Sigal, Soffer–Weinstein, Gang–Sigal, etc.) and the linear relation between S-matrix poles and resonance widths. No source located formulates or solves the inverse problem of recovering the nonlinear FGR constant or the nonlinear resonance positions from the nonlinear S-matrix for a double-well potential plus nonlinearity; the question appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Fermi's golden rule - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Describes the linear FGR rate for transitions to the continuum; no inverse-scattering recovery is discussed.
status_evidence.claim: Standard FGR formulations concern the direct (forward) problem, not recovery from the S-matrix in the nonlinear setting.

status_evidence.title: The Gamow and the Fermi Golden Rules
status_evidence.snippet: For long-lived resonances the exact Gamow Golden Rule reduces to the approximate Fermi Golden Rule, with widths tied to imaginary parts of S-matrix poles.
status_evidence.claim: Links between S-matrix poles and FGR widths are established only in the linear setting.
